claims.text: Pre-sintering vapor deposition can form a thin, uniform, conformal Cu layer on tungsten surfaces.
A uniform Cu coating on tungsten facilitates enhanced interparticle bonding during sintering.
The pre-deposited Cu layer improves local wettability during sintering.
Improved local wettability reduces void formation in the W–Cu composite.
The Cu pre-coating reduces phase separation during sintering.
The Cu pre-coating promotes more intimate and uniform contact at W–Cu interfaces.
Cu-pre-coated W–Cu composites will have higher thermal conductivity than conventionally cast or sintered composites without Cu pre-coating.
Cu-pre-coated W–Cu composites will have greater mechanical strength than W–Cu composites made by spark-plasma sintering, mechanical alloying, or direct infiltration without Cu pre-coating.
The proposed processing route is effective below the melting point of tungsten when oxidation is prevented.
The resulting composite is suitable for high-thermal-load applications such as fusion-reactor joints.
